O.content: The title reads "Advertising Budget vs Revenue (High-Performing Regions)".
Only five labeled points, January through May, are visible, and no marks or labels for other regional groups are visible.

B.text: If a broader budget increase requires evidence from regions beyond the displayed high-performing subset or evidence that budget increases caused revenue increases, then a chart limited to that subset and showing only plotted monthly association is insufficient, supporting a request for full-data analysis.
B.conditions: Applies if approval requires representative regional coverage or causal/full-data validation.

O.content: The title reads "Advertising Budget vs Revenue (High-Performing Regions)".
The horizontal-axis inscription reads "Advertising Budget ($)" and its printed ticks increase from 0 at the left toward 70 at the right.
The vertical-axis inscription reads "Revenue ($)" and its printed ticks increase from 0 at the bottom toward 220 near the top.
Five blue points are labeled January, February, March, April, and May; from January through May, each successive labeled point is farther right and higher on the page than the preceding point.

B.text: If the horizontal and vertical axes encode advertising budget and revenue respectively, with values increasing rightward and upward, then the labeled monthly points form a positive budget-revenue association; if the review permits broader approval from this high-performing-region association alone, it supports approval.
B.conditions: Applies only if the plotted points are comparable monthly observations for the stated high-performing regions and association is sufficient evidence for a broader increase.
